name: SDN Host Storage Ingest Node
description: Host storage.ingest_with_source connector (typed contracts 1.0). Method "ingest": the parser's IngestRequest (INGQ, module-sdk runtime type: SCHEMA, TAGS SourceTags, RECONCILE, ARCHIVE, PROVENANCE) on "meta", the batch's size-prefixed SDS record stream on the "<code>_records" port of its standard (one port per standard, since a typed port names one type: omm, mpe, cat, spw, eop, csm, egp, sit, lcc, tbs, gnp, wxf, cnp, rfb, iqc, tct, dtt, ldm, ocm, obd, pce, pnm, oem, dcl) and, optionally, the HttpResponse (HRSP) the batch was made from on "raw" become ONE storage.ingest_with_source hostcall, sent as an SDS $PIV invocation: the StorageIngestParams aligned record (flat source tags, RECONCILE, ARCHIVE_SOURCE/ARCHIVE_NAME), raw "records", raw "archive" (the HttpResponse BODY, only when the request names an ARCHIVE target) and list "provenance" (one Provenance aligned record). It answers ONE IngestResult (INGR) on "result". Aligned strings are bounded (SOURCE_URL 255, BATCH_ID 128, ...): a value that does not fit is never truncated - the batch is answered with REFUSED naming the field, and nothing is stored. A host refusal (policy, disk guardrail, capability grant) is answered the same way; any other host failure fails the node. No JSON and no base64. Host-side behavior is policy-mediated by the dedicated storage_ingest capability grant (disk guardrail, batch store with source tags, source-batch reconcile, raw/provenance archiving).

externalInterfaces.description: Provenance/batch-capable record ingest through the host storage.ingest_with_source hostcall, sent as an SDS $PIV invocation (StorageIngestParams + raw records/archive + list provenance; sdn-server modulert/caps/storage.go).

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (module-sdk runtime type INGQ): SCHEMA (the records' standard, e.g. "WXF.fbs"), TAGS (SourceTags: PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID, SOURCE_URL, CONTENT_KEY_ID, SOURCE_PEER, LICENSE, LICENSE_URL, CITATION, SHARE_ALIKE), RECONCILE (Duplicates default | None | Current), optional ARCHIVE (SOURCE, NAME) and PROVENANCE.

inputPorts.description: The batch's ingest request (attribution, reconcile mode, archive naming, provenance), authored by the parser node.

inputPorts.description: The record batch when the IngestRequest's SCHEMA is OMM.fbs. EXACTLY ONE *_records port carries a frame per invocation, and it must be the SCHEMA's.

methods.description: Persists one provenance-attributed record batch through the policy-mediated storage.ingest_with_source hostcall (typed: SDS $PIV). BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. Merging is NOT the safe reading for this node: the IngestRequest's batch id, archive naming and provenance were computed over exactly one records stream and one raw document, so a second records frame would make the request describe bytes it was never computed over.

sequentialJustification.detail: Serial generic storage host I/O; host owns concurrency.
